subject.title: fix: strip volatile output from exec result hash to fix no-progress detection (#93917)

question: Should loop detection treat repeated same-command nonzero exec outcomes with identical structured exit identity as no progress even when their output changes?
rationale: The rule fixes the demonstrated runaway loop but can deliberately classify changing nonzero output as equivalent, so the acceptable false-positive versus runaway-loop tradeoff is an agent-runtime ownership decision.

options.title: Accept stable nonzero equivalence
options.body: Land the current structured fingerprint after rebasing because it fixes the reproduced runaway-loop path while preserving exit-zero output as progress.

options.title: Narrow the equivalence rule
options.body: Revise the fingerprint to retain selected output-derived distinctions or limit normalization to specific failure classes, accepting weaker protection from volatile-output loops.

recommendation.title: Accept stable nonzero equivalence
recommendation.body: Land the current structured fingerprint after rebasing because it fixes the reproduced runaway-loop path while preserving exit-zero output as progress.
